title: UK Unmarried Partner Visa | Manchester Immigration Advisers
description: Unmarried partner visa help for couples who have lived together for 2 years. IAA-regulated advice on cohabitation evidence and the financial requirement.
intro: If you are in a long-term relationship with a British or settled partner but not married, you can apply as an unmarried partner. The key is proving you have lived together in a relationship like a marriage. We prepare your unmarried partner visa application, including the evidence of living together.
eligibility: You have lived together in a relationship akin to marriage for the required period
You both intend to live together permanently in the UK
You meet the financial and English language requirements

faqs.q: What counts as proof we lived together?
faqs.a: Official letters addressed to you both at the same address, spread over the period, are strongest. We review what you have and tell you where the gaps are.

faqs.q: We have lived together for less than 2 years. What can we do?
faqs.a: You may be able to marry and apply as spouses, or apply for a fiancé(e) visa if you plan to marry in the UK. We can explain the options.

faqs.q: How long does an unmarried partner visa take?
faqs.a: Applications from outside the UK are usually decided within about 12 weeks, and from inside the UK within about 8 weeks.

sections.heading: Who can apply as an unmarried partner?
sections.text: If you aren't married or in a civil partnership, you can still apply as a couple if you have lived together in a relationship similar to marriage for at least 2 years before you apply. Your UK partner must be British, Irish, settled in the UK, or have protected status.

sections.heading: Proving you have lived together for 2 years
sections.text:
This is the hardest part for most couples. The Home Office expects documents addressed to you both, or to each of you, at the same address, spread across the full 2 years. Useful evidence includes:
- A joint tenancy agreement or mortgage
- Utility, council tax or broadband bills
- Bank statements and official letters
- Photos and travel records over time

Short gaps can usually be explained, but gaps in the evidence are a common reason for refusal.

sections.heading: Other requirements
sections.text: Unmarried partners must meet the same financial, English language and accommodation requirements as spouses: usually £29,000 a year for a new application, English at A1 level, and suitable accommodation without public funds. The route leads to settlement in the same way as a spouse visa.

sections.heading: Unmarried partner visa help in Manchester
